name: ARIES
question: Does once-daily mirabegron reduce incontinence episodes and micturition frequency versus placebo in adults with overactive bladder?

design.population: Adults in the United States and Canada with overactive bladder symptoms for at least three months.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 randomized trial
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods; publisher article, Patient Disposition and Demographics; FDA clinical review p93, Figure 3

verdictNote: Both doses met both co-primary symptom endpoints versus placebo at 12 weeks.
takeaway: In ARIES, mirabegron 50 mg and 100 mg once daily each reduced incontinence episodes and micturitions more than placebo over 12 weeks in adults with overactive bladder.

reports.label: Primary 12-week report
reports.citation: Nitti VW, Auerbach S, Martin N, et al. "Results of a randomized phase III trial of mirabegron in patients with overactive bladder." *J Urol.* 2013;189(4):1388-1395. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2012.10.017

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to final visit (95% CI)
results.note: Both mirabegron doses differed significantly from placebo; intervals are for within-arm mean changes.

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to final visit (95% CI)
results.note: Both mirabegron doses differed significantly from placebo; intervals are for within-arm mean changes.

harms.label: Dry mouth
harms.note: The abstract reports percentages without event counts or denominators.

harms.label: Frequently reported treatment-emergent adverse events
harms.note: Hypertension, urinary tract infection, headache, and nasopharyngitis had similar incidence across mirabegron and placebo groups; no rates are given in the abstract.

delivery.label: Treatment schedule
delivery.value: Two-week placebo run-in, then mirabegron 50 mg, mirabegron 100 mg, or placebo once daily for 12 weeks.

relations.note: Companion phase 3 mirabegron trial in Europe, Australia, and South Africa with a tolterodine reference arm.
